document.title: Impressions of Waziristan (Islamabad 00919)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), "No-Go" Tribal Areas Became Basis for Afghan Insurgency Documents Show
document.note: [Confidential] Summarizes conditions in Waziristan. Pakistan faces a daunting military and political challenge driving foreign fighters from North and South Waziristan and integrating the areas. Authority has shifted from maliks to mullahs, opening the region to foreign extremists, and Pakistani officials see development aid as the way to keep the maliks loyal. The page notes Islamabad funded religious parties in the tribal areas in the 1980s for the anti-Soviet campaign.

events.description: Poloff accompanied Congressman Mark Kirk on a Pakistan military-sponsored visit to the capitals of North and South Waziristan; briefings, a forward position overlooking the Shakai Valley, and a meeting with Waziri maliks.
U.S. Embassy Islamabad cable 'Impressions of Waziristan' sent to State Department.
GOP decision to actively recruit Waziris and Mehsuds for the jihad in Soviet-occupied Afghanistan, disrupting the maliks' balance of authority.
After the defeat of the Taliban, religious leaders in the Waziristans convinced tribes to open territories to Taliban remnants and foreign supporters.
New Pakistan military offensive in Mehsud areas.
Poloff accompanied Congressman Mark Kirk on a Pakistan military-sponsored visit to the capitals of North and South Waziristan, including Wana and a forward position overlooking Shakai Valley.
Delegation met briefly with local Waziri maliks in South Waziristan.
Embassy Islamabad cable 'Impressions of Waziristan' sent to State Department under Ambassador Crocker.
GOP decision to recruit Waziris and Mehsuds for jihad against the Soviets in Afghanistan, empowering Deobandi and JI leaders over maliks.
Pakistani military offensive in Mehsud areas following earlier operations against foreign fighters in Waziri areas.

key_claims: GOP recruitment of Waziris and Mehsuds for the anti-Soviet jihad undermined the traditional authority of maliks.
Deobandi and Jamaat-e-Islami religious leaders usurped malik authority and connected tribes to the Taliban.
After the Taliban's defeat, religious leaders persuaded tribes to host Taliban remnants and foreign supporters in the Waziristans.
Pakistani military strategy aims to restore maliks, using arrests and collective punishment under the FCR.
Military operations in South Waziristan were judged successful in driving a wedge between foreign fighters and tribal hosts.
Development assistance is seen as key to retaining maliks' loyalty and integrating FATA into Pakistan.
